scope: Country-level agricultural evidence, source inventory, data-quality notes and missing farm-budget inputs. This is not a calculator profile and does not authorize country activation.

geographic_coverage.campaign_period: December 2023 to November 2024 for crop production; livestock reference period May 2024 to April 2025

values.indicator: Holdings primarily producing for own consumption

key_evidence.source: INSEED RGA-2 2025 results, based on the 2023-2024 agricultural census
key_evidence.caveat: National structural indicators. The 0.40 ha average and high prevalence of small holdings mean national averages must not be treated as representative commercial farm sizes.

values.reported_rank: second largest food crop by production

key_evidence.caveat: These are national campaign totals. The public results summary does not expose all crop-specific area denominators, island-level tables or the complete crop list; do not calculate farm yields by dividing these totals by an unrelated land-area figure.
Selected figures reported in the public summary only. Verify crop-specific denominator, island, production system and weighting in detailed census tables before use in farm budgets.

values.indicator: Share of agricultural holdings with livestock

key_evidence.caveat: National stock counts only. No verified commercial broiler/layer split, liveweight, breed, productivity, feed conversion, mortality, farm-gate sale price or input-cost series recorded here.

values.indicator: Fertilized area using combined organic and mineral fertilizer

key_evidence.caveat: The fertilizer percentages are shares of fertilized area, not shares of all cultivated land.

key_evidence.reference_period: 2021 household-level survey; FAO policy brief published 2023
key_evidence.source: FAO Agricultural Development Economics Policy Brief No. 69, Agricultural yields and production in the Comoros
key_evidence.caveat: FAO reports that banana and cassava are the most important crops by production and yield, and that yields for many crops were low relative to international averages. This is an older 2021 survey and must not be substituted for the newer RGA-2 census results.

key_evidence.source: FAO, Unveiling the agricultural landscape of the Comoros: An analysis of agricultural production and yields
key_evidence.caveat: Useful for interpreting crop production and yield distributions, but the underlying survey is from 2021. Use alongside, not instead of, the 2023-2024 RGA-2 census.

key_evidence.source: World Bank indicator page citing FAOSTAT
key_evidence.caveat: Aggregate cereal-yield indicator, not a crop-specific yield or a farm-level observation. Do not use as a maize, rice or other individual crop yield.

data_quality_and_use: The RGA-2 is the strongest current national structural source identified in this review. It was conducted by INSEED with FAO technical support and World Bank financing.
The RGA-2 public microdata catalogue records version 1.0, dated 15 April 2026, and describes the released files as cleaned, weighted and validated by the technical committee.
The census is a national campaign source; island-specific results and crop-level denominator tables must be checked before deriving regional yields or budgets.
Production totals, yields, retail prices, farm-gate prices and input costs are different measures and must remain separately labelled.
No current verified farm-gate commodity prices or detailed crop enterprise budgets were established from the sources reviewed.

missing_data_before_calculator_use: Current island- and district-specific farm-gate prices for target crops, with date, market, grade and unit.
Current retail market price series kept separate from producer prices.
Crop-specific harvested area and yield distributions for banana, cassava, sweet potato, rice, maize, vegetables, vanilla, clove and ylang-ylang, by island where possible.
Farmer-paid seed and planting-material costs, fertilizer and manure costs, crop-protection costs, labour rates and labour requirements.
Irrigation, water, energy, land preparation, tools, machinery hire, transport, packaging, storage and post-harvest costs.
Crop cycle length, planting density, harvest frequency, marketable share, losses and farm-gate grade differentials.
Livestock species/breed production systems, feed costs, veterinary costs, mortality, productivity and dated sale prices.
Independent validation of census table definitions, weights and crop-specific denominators before converting national observations into enterprise budgets.
recommendation: Retain Comoros as research-only. The national census provides a substantial evidence base for agricultural structure, production and livestock, but the currently identified public evidence does not establish a complete, current farm-level cost and farm-gate price dataset. Do not activate a Comoros calculator profile or infer profitability until the missing budget inputs are sourced and validated.
